meta.title: Otaku Japan
meta.sources: Cross-referenced from the Google Maps export: favorites and want-to-go lists, the saved places sheet, and the Otaku/Arcades/Music/Thrift + film-sites layers of the private My Maps.

akihabara.label: Neon Akihabara
akihabara.story: Day one is the pilgrimage, but the shops wait — this day is the district itself. Katsu curry at Hinoya under the tracks, the FFXIV cafe in the Pasela building, the robot-staffed cafe, the owl cafe, taiyaki off Chuo-dori. When the sun drops the signage does the work — and if the night runs long, MOGRA is a basement by the tracks where the DJs play anison to people who know every word.

godzilla.label: The Godzilla Trail
godzilla.sub: Seventy years of the King, walking distance apart
godzilla.story: Its own map because it deserves one. The Wako clock tower he flattened in Minus One, the Hibiya statue that replaced the 1995 original, the Diet Building where the cabinet argued while he approached, the Nakagin site on the way through Ginza. Then Kabukicho: the head over the Toho Building roars on the hour, the Godzilla Store is a block away, and Square Enix HQ sits on the east side. Tokyo Tower counts too; he has wrecked it more than once.

pilgrimage.label: The Anime Pilgrimage
pilgrimage.sub: Reze arc, Shibuya Incident, Shinkai, the ghoul wards
pilgrimage.story: One map, four Tokyos drawn over the real one. The Reze arc is a Jinbocho afternoon: the phone booth in the storm, the cafe hers was modeled on, the stone stairs where fans leave gerbera flowers. The Shibuya Incident has its own blocks — the crossing, the 109, the B5F platform. Suga Shrine's stairs and the Yotsuya bridge are Shinkai's. And the ghoul wards run underneath all of it.

gaming.label: Gaming & Arcades
gaming.story: The cabinet map. Super Potato's retro floors and the candy arcade on top, GiGO and HEY holding the Electric Town arcade line, Mikado in Takadanobaba where the old guard still runs tournaments. Joypolis on the bay, the esports park inside Tokyo Tower, and the two tiny arcade museums in Toshima and Sugamo for the pre-history.

shibuya.label: The Harajuku–Daikanyama Walk
shibuya.sub: Cat Street to the manga floor
shibuya.story: The walk day. Takeshita's crepe chaos into the quieter Cat Street, then south to Daikanyama T-Site: the best English manga floor in the city, Akira storyboard books in the art stacks, and Anjin upstairs with the leather chairs to read the haul. The day ends there, at dusk, on purpose.

odaiba.label: Odaiba & the Bay
odaiba.story: Take the Yurikamome over Rainbow Bridge — the Weathering with You shot — and spend a day on the artificial island. The Unicorn Gundam transforms on schedule outside DiverCity. The miniature world of Small Worlds, then teamLab Planets at Toyosu where you wade barefoot through the art, or Borderless at Azabudai.

museums.label: The Museum Arc
museums.sub: Ghibli to Tokiwaso, the industry's memory
museums.story: The museum day out along the Chuo and Odakyu lines. The Ghibli Museum in Mitaka is lottery-ticket only and worth the planning. Fujiko F Fujio's museum in Kawasaki has the original Doraemon art. Sanrio Puroland is the pink overload. Tokiwaso rebuilds the apartment where Tezuka and the Fujikos invented the industry, and Suginami's free museum sits where the studios are. Ikebukuro's rooftop garden is the pause in the middle.

yokohama.label: Yokohama
yokohama.story: Half an hour south. The Red Brick Warehouse that Godzilla flattened in Minus One, Cosmoworld's wheel on the water, Chinatown for lunch, and the Gundam Base satellite on the harbor. The Ramen Museum at Shin-Yokohama doubles as the train home.

fuji.label: Fuji-Q Excursion
fuji.story: The optional detour, for a clear day. Fuji-Q has world-tier coasters and a permanent Hidden Leaf village, Ichiraku ramen included, with the mountain looming behind the Hokage faces. Bus from Shinjuku, back in time for dinner.

nagoya.label: Ghibli Park
nagoya.story: The shinkansen west stops being transport and becomes part of the trip here. Ghibli Park sits on the old Expo grounds outside Nagoya: no rides, just built worlds. Kiki's bakery, Satsuki and Mei's house, the Grand Warehouse. Timed entry, so this day is planned, not improvised.

osaka.label: Osaka
osaka.story: Osaka's otaku district is Denden Town in Nipponbashi, rougher and more local than Akihabara: Animate, Jungle, figure and card shops, the Good Smile collab cafe. The FFXIV Eorzea Cafe is in Dotonbori, five minutes from the Glico sign. The castle in the morning — Godzilla wrecked it in 1955 — Kuromon market for lunch, Nipponbashi until the legs give out. JOJOPUB is a thirty-minute hop up to Kyoto if the night calls for it.

usj.label: Universal Studios Japan
usj.story: The park day. Super Nintendo World is the reason: punch the blocks, ride Mario Kart, eat at Kinopio's. The anime collabs rotate through the rest of the park, One Piece and Monster Hunter lately. Express Pass buys back hours; book it early.

kobe.label: Kobe Stopover
kobe.sub: Sake town on the way south
kobe.story: The decompression stop between Osaka and the island. Kobe's Nada district is sake country: Hakutsuru's brewery museum and Shushinkan's tasting counter are twenty minutes apart on foot. Sleep by the harbor; the bridge to Awaji is tomorrow.

awaji.label: Awaji Island
awaji.sub: The island. Nijigen no Mori, Godzilla, the Kitty coast
awaji.story: The finale, and it earns the position. Awaji is its own place: a forest park across the Akashi Kaikyo bridge where someone built the anime island. Nijigen no Mori holds the Hidden Leaf, Dragon Quest Island, and a Godzilla you zipline into. The Godzilla Museum is beside it. On the west coast, Hello Kitty Smile and Show Box face the strait, and the onion burgers at Uzunooka sit under the Naruto bridge. Stay the night on the island if you can.

return.label: The Way Home
return.story: Awaji is the far shore, so the trip home is engineered, not endured. The suitcases go ahead by takkyubin courier from the island to the Tokyo hotel, so you cross the Akashi Kaikyo bridge with a day pack. Kobe Airport is twenty minutes from the bridge bus, the hop to Haneda is barely an hour, and the bags beat you to the room.

lastday.label: The Last Day — The Shopping Run
lastday.sub: Every store, one day, with a list
lastday.story: You never shop at the beginning of a trip. You shop at the end, with a list — and this is the list. Every store you scouted all trip, one map: the Akihabara wall of Radio Kaikan, Kotobukiya, Mandarake and Animate; Nakano Broadway's secondhand floors; Ikebukuro's flagships and the gashapon hall; Parco's sixth floor, the Harajuku vintage shops, the Gundam Base. Then Character Street for the giftable pile before the airport.

shop-akiba.label: Akihabara — figures, games, the retro wall

shop-ikebukuro.label: Ikebukuro — flagships and the gashapon hall

shop-bay.label: The bay — Gundam Base, last Gunpla stop

beats.title: The map is the plan
beats.text: Two weeks rebuilt out of a decade of saved pins. Tokyo first, because most of the life is there. Then the shinkansen west through Nagoya to Osaka, out to Universal, over the bridge to Awaji Island, and back to Tokyo for the last shopping day.

beats.title: Tokyo, the base
beats.text: Tokyo gets the bulk of the days, inside the Yamanote loop and out into the west suburbs. Each map below is its own world at its own scale: the districts, then the pilgrimages.

beats.title: The shinkansen west
beats.text: Bags packed, seat on the right side for the Fuji view. The Tokaido line is the oldest high-speed rail on earth and still the best way to cross the country. Nagoya for Ghibli Park, then Osaka.

beats.title: Kansai
beats.text: Osaka is a different tempo: louder, cheaper, hungrier. The otaku district is Denden Town; the castle is the morning; Dotonbori is the evening.

beats.title: The island
beats.text: Awaji is not a district of anything. It is its own place, sitting in the strait between Honshu and Shikoku, and for this trip it is the destination, not a day trip. The anime park, the Godzilla, the Kitty coast, the onions.

spots.name: AKIHABARA KOTOBUKIYA
spots.blurb: Five floors of figures, kits and character goods a minute from the Electric Town exit. The 1F bargain bins are where the weird stuff hides.

spots.name: Akihabara Radio Kaikan
spots.blurb: The yellow box by the station. Ten floors: K-Books, amiami, Volks, Kaiyodo. If a hobby exists, someone in this building sells its merch.

spots.name: Mandarake Complex
spots.blurb: Eight floors of black walls and secondhand treasure. Doujin, vintage toys, cel art, cosplay. The floor guide alone is a museum of fandom.

spots.name: Animate Akihabara
spots.blurb: The mainline anime store, split across two buildings. New releases, exclusive bonuses, and seasonal pop-ups on the event floor.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田四丁目３番２号

spots.name: Akiba Cultures Zone
spots.blurb: A multi-floor otaku mall that rotates tenants. Figures, cards, idols, whatever the current wave is.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田一丁目７番６号

spots.name: Super Potato Akihabara
spots.blurb: The retro game temple. Three floors of Famicom to Dreamcast, then a candy-and-crt arcade on top. The intro jingle lives in your head rent free.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田一丁目１１番２号

spots.name: GiGO Akihabara Building 3
spots.blurb: A survivor of the Sega building purge. Rhythm games, fighters and UFO catchers across several floors.

spots.name: HEY (Hirose Entertainment Yard)
spots.blurb: Taito's showcase arcade across the street. Serious fighting game floors upstairs, rows of crane games below.

spots.name: D.D.R AKIBA
spots.blurb: Record shop for anison, game music and idol vinyl. The Akihabara soundtrack in physical form.

spots.name: TAMASHII NATIONS STORE TOKYO
spots.blurb: Bandai's collector brand flagship. The glass cases of Soul of Chogokin and Figuarts are closer to a gallery than a store.

spots.name: COSPA Akihabara
spots.blurb: The otaku apparel and goods maker's own shop. Character tees, jackets, and the kind of merchandise that reads subtle to anyone outside the loop.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田三丁目１５番５号

spots.name: MOGRA
spots.blurb: The anison and netlabel club in a basement by the tracks. DJs play anime songs and game remixes to a floor of people who know every word. Saved from the favorites list.
spots.matched: 東京都台東区秋葉原３番１１号

spots.name: Hinoya Curry Akihabara
spots.blurb: The katsu curry institution. Order at the ticket machine, get a fried cutlet over rice drowned in dark curry. Fast, loud, perfect.

spots.name: Kyushu Jangara Akihabara
spots.blurb: Tonkotsu ramen on the main drag. The all-toppings bowl is the classic tourist move and it earns it.

spots.name: Eorzea Cafe Akihabara
spots.blurb: The Final Fantasy XIV cafe in the Pasela building. Job cocktails, moogle desserts, and dishes named after raids. Reservations recommended.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田一丁目１番１０号

spots.name: Owl Cafe Tokyo
spots.blurb: A tiny owl cafe off the main street. Hourly slots, small groups, actual owls. Saved in the list, worth booking ahead.

spots.name: EXBAR TOKYO plus Akihabara
spots.blurb: Retro game bar near the station. Cabinets, cartridges behind the counter, and drinks named after boss fights.

spots.name: Naruto Taiyaki Asakusabashi
spots.blurb: The taiyaki shop from the naruto-district name, not the ninja. Crisp skin, red bean or custard, still warm from the iron. A short hop east of Akihabara.
spots.matched: 東京都台東区浅草橋一丁目１７番

spots.name: DAWN Avatar Robot Cafe
spots.blurb: The cafe where the servers are remote-operated robots piloted by people who cannot leave home. One of the most quietly radical things you can do in Tokyo.

spots.name: Tokyo Character Street
spots.blurb: The underground mall inside Tokyo Station's Yaesu side. Pokemon Store, Jump Shop, Ghibli, Rilakkuma, Miffy. Twenty shops in a row before your shinkansen even leaves.

spots.name: Anime Tokyo Station
spots.blurb: A small anime exhibit space inside Tokyo Station Ichibangai. Rotating displays and event corners. Free to wander.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区丸の内一丁目９番

spots.name: Nakano Broadway
spots.blurb: The other mecca. Four floors of Mandarake branches, watch shops, idol goods, taco-che books and crumbling Showa charm. The building Otomo drew in Steins;Gate territory.

spots.name: Mandarake Nakano
spots.blurb: Technically dozens of Mandarake micro-shops inside Broadway, each a different obsession. The anime cel and vintage toy floors are the draw.

spots.name: Nakano Sun Mall
spots.blurb: The covered arcade between the station and Broadway. Taiyaki, standing sushi, and the slow reveal of Broadway's facade at the end.

spots.name: animate Ikebukuro
spots.blurb: The largest anime store on earth after the 2023 expansion. Nine floors of manga, goods, and event space near Otome Road.

spots.name: Evangelion Store Ikebukuro
spots.blurb: EVA-specific merch in the Parco-adjacent block. Plugsuit everything.

spots.name: Gashapon Ikebukuro
spots.blurb: The world's largest capsule toy store, verified by Guinness. Thousands of machines. Bring coins and resolve.

spots.name: Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo & Pikachu Sweets
spots.blurb: The flagship Pokemon Center in Sunshine City, with Pikachu Sweets next door. The line for seasonal plush starts early.
spots.matched: Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo & Pikachu Sweets

spots.name: Animate Annex
spots.blurb: The second Ikebukuro Animate, mostly merchandise. Quieter than the flagship, same loyalty points.

spots.name: Tokiwaso Manga Museum
spots.blurb: A reconstruction of the apartment where Tezuka, Fujiko Fujio and the manga gods lived in the 50s. The birthplace of the industry, rebuilt down to the tatami.

spots.name: Dagashiya Game Museum
spots.blurb: A candy-store museum up in Toshima with playable retro cabinets and Showa junk food. Small, strange, wonderful.

spots.name: Natsuge Museum
spots.blurb: A retro arcade museum in Sugamo. Early cabinets, pachinko-era machines, the stuff before the stuff.

spots.name: A Happy Pancake Ikebukuro
spots.blurb: The souffle pancake place. Twenty minutes of jiggle per order. A good pause between stores.
spots.matched: 東京都豊島区南池袋一丁目１８番

spots.name: Ikebukuro Seibu Rooftop
spots.blurb: The department store roof garden with a Monet water-lily pond replica. The calmest square meter in Ikebukuro.
spots.matched: 東京都豊島区南池袋一丁目２８番１号

spots.name: Shibuya Parco
spots.blurb: The sixth floor is the real draw: Nintendo Tokyo, Pokemon Center Shibuya, the Jump Shop, Capcom Store, all in one strip. The building that turned a mall into a console war detente.

spots.name: Mandarake Shibuya
spots.blurb: The Shibuya branch underground on Inokashira-dori. Smaller than Nakano but curated weird.

spots.name: Toy Sapiens
spots.blurb: Hot Toys flagship. Movie-accurate figures at movie-poster prices. Worth it just to see the craftsmanship.

spots.name: J-Pop Cafe
spots.blurb: A themed cafe spot saved from the film-locations list. Check what the current collaboration is before going.

spots.name: Takeshita Street
spots.blurb: The crepe-and-chaos alley off Harajuku Station. Also a JJK and Tokyo Drift filming point, per the film map data.

spots.name: Cat Street
spots.blurb: The quieter walk from Harajuku into Shibuya. Vintage and streetwear shops, the fashion side of the same subculture coin.

spots.name: Kinji Used Clothing Harajuku
spots.blurb: Big vintage floor under the Harajuku streetscape. Same instinct as the Koenji thrift circuit, bigger selection.

spots.name: RAGTAG Harajuku
spots.blurb: Designer resale. The floor where a Comme des Garcons jacket costs less than a new hoodie.

spots.name: DAIKANYAMA T-SITE
spots.blurb: Where the Shibuya day ends. The Tsutaya at Daikanyama carries the best English-language manga selection in the city, and the art stacks hold storyboard books and film panels, Akira among them. Upstairs, the Anjin lounge is the reward: leather chairs, low light, a proper drink while you read what you just bought. Come at dusk, stay until closing.

spots.name: Unicorn Gundam Statue
spots.blurb: The life-size transforming Unicorn outside DiverCity. It shifts to destroy mode on a schedule with lights and the horn opening. Still the best free show on the bay.
spots.matched: 東京都江東区青海一丁目１番１０号

spots.name: The Gundam Base Tokyo
spots.blurb: The Gunpla flagship inside DiverCity 7F. Limited kits, a build space, and the most dangerous wall of boxes in Tokyo for a modeler.
spots.matched: 東京都江東区青海一丁目１番１０号

spots.name: Tokyo Joypolis
spots.blurb: Sega's indoor park at Decks. Half-pipe rides, VR coasters, the arcade floor stays loud.

spots.name: small worlds miniature museum
spots.blurb: The miniature museum in Ariake. Evangelion's Tokyo-3 in 1:80, a moving space center, an airport with departing planes. The detail level is absurd.

spots.name: teamLab Planets
spots.blurb: The barefoot digital art maze in Toyosu. Wading through knee-deep water projections. Timed tickets, sells out.

spots.name: teamLab Borderless
spots.blurb: The reborn Borderless at Azabudai Hills. Rooms that bleed into each other, no map, no wrong way.
spots.matched: teamLab Borderless: MORI Building DIGITAL ART MUSEUM

spots.name: Rainbow Bridge (Weathering with You)
spots.blurb: The bridge Hina and Hodaka cross as the sky clears. The Yurikamome ride over it is the cheapest bay view in Tokyo.

spots.name: RED° Tokyo Tower
spots.blurb: The esports park inside Tokyo Tower's foot building. Retro floor, VR, sim rigs. The tower itself still earns the trip up.

spots.name: Ghibli Museum
spots.blurb: The Mitaka museum. Tickets only by advance lottery, no photos inside, a real Catbus you can climb. The Saturn Theater short is worth the trip alone.

spots.name: Fujiko F Fujio Museum
spots.blurb: The Doraemon museum in Kawasaki. Original art, a rooftop with the anywhere door, and the kindest museum staff in the prefecture.

spots.name: Sanrio Puroland
spots.blurb: The indoor Hello Kitty theme park in Tama. Fully covered, aggressively pink, the boat ride is genuinely charming.
spots.matched: 東京都多摩市落合一丁目３１番地

spots.name: Suginami Animation Museum
spots.blurb: Free museum in Ogikubo covering how anime is actually made, with dubbing booths and a small theater. Suginami is where the studios are.
spots.matched: Tokyo Polytechnic University Suginami Animation Museum

spots.name: Takadanobaba Mikado
spots.blurb: The fighting game arcade that outlived everything. Tournaments, legacy cabinets, the old guard still plays here.

spots.name: Gundam Base Yokohama satellite
spots.blurb: The satellite Gunpla shop by the waterfront. The moving Gundam at the Factory ended in 2024, but the store remains.
spots.matched: 神奈川県横浜市中区新港二丁目

spots.name: Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse
spots.blurb: The warehouse Godzilla flattens in Minus One. Now craft beer and event halls. The bay walk here is the best in Yokohama.
spots.matched: Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse (Godzilla Minus One)

spots.name: Yokohama Cosmoworld
spots.blurb: The waterfront amusement park with the clock ferris wheel. Free entry, pay per ride, open late.
spots.matched: 神奈川県横浜市中区新港二丁目８番

spots.name: Yokohama Chinatown
spots.blurb: The biggest Chinatown in Japan. Steam buns on every corner, the Kanteibyo temple at the center.

spots.name: Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum
spots.blurb: The underground Showa streetscape of regional ramen shops. Half-portion bowls let you eat through the map. One stop from the shinkansen at Shin-Yokohama.

spots.name: Autobacs ASM Yokohama
spots.blurb: The legendary GT-R tuner shop. Car culture otaku territory, not anime, but the garage energy is the same.
spots.matched: 神奈川県横浜市保土ケ谷区川島町

spots.name: Fuji-Q Highland
spots.blurb: The coaster park at the mountain's foot. Eejanaika and Fujiyama are still among the world's best steel.

spots.name: NARUTO×BORUTO FUJI HIDDEN VILLAGE OF KONOHA
spots.blurb: The Hidden Leaf land inside Fuji-Q. Ichiraku ramen, shinobi missions, and Mount Fuji photobombing the Hokage monument.
spots.matched: NARUTO×BORUTO FUJI HIDDEN VILLAGE OF KONOHA

spots.name: Ghibli Park
spots.blurb: The Ghibli park on the old Expo grounds in Nagakute. No rides, just walks through built worlds: the bakery from Kiki, Satsuki and Mei's house, the Grand Warehouse. Timed entry, plan ahead.
spots.matched: 愛知県長久手市茨ケ廻間乙１５３３番地

spots.name: Nipponbashi Denden Town
spots.blurb: Osaka's Akihabara, on Nipponbashi-suji. Animate, Super Potato, Jungle, figure shops, maid cafes, card shops. More local, less tourist-polished.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市浪速区日本橋四丁目１５番

spots.name: JOJOPUB
spots.blurb: A JoJo's Bizarre Adventure themed bar, thirty minutes up the line in Kyoto. Stand-named cocktails and owner enthusiasm. Worth the hop on a Denden Town evening.

spots.name: Eorzea Cafe Osaka
spots.blurb: The Osaka branch of the FFXIV cafe in Dotonbori's Pasela building. Same menu cycle, easier to book than Akihabara.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市中央区道頓堀一丁目４番２７号

spots.name: Good Smile x Animate Cafe Osaka
spots.blurb: The rotating-collab cafe in Nipponbashi. Whatever property is running that month gets the menu, the coasters, the whole room.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市浪速区日本橋四丁目１５番１７号

spots.name: Osaka Castle
spots.blurb: The castle on the hill that Godzilla wrecked in 1955. The park around it is Osaka's best skyline frame.

spots.name: The Landmark Square Osaka
spots.blurb: The restaurant complex in the old Osaka Castle park buildings. Good lunch stop after the castle keep.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市中央区大阪城３番１号

spots.name: Dotonbori
spots.blurb: The neon canal strip. The Glico runner, takoyaki on every corner, kushikatsu rules about double dipping enforced by signage.

spots.name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
spots.blurb: Osaka's market street. Scallops grilled in the shell, wagyu skewers, fruit you cannot afford. Eat walking.

spots.name: National Bunraku Theatre
spots.blurb: The puppet theater near Nipponbashi. Three-person puppets performing tragedy, centuries before anime perfected the same faces.

spots.name: Umeda Sky Building
spots.blurb: The floating garden observatory. The escalator through the sky is the shot.

spots.name: Takimikoji
spots.blurb: The retro Showa food street in the Sky Building basement. Cheap lunch in a film set.

spots.name: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living
spots.blurb: The museum with a full-size Edo street indoors, sky effects overhead. Walk a 19th century Osaka block in yukata.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市北区天神橋六丁目４番２０号

spots.name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
spots.blurb: One of the world's great aquariums, built around a central Pacific tank with a whale shark. On the bay, pairs with the USJ side.

spots.name: teamLab Botanical Garden Osaka
spots.blurb: The night botanical garden in Nagai Park. Art projected onto real trees. Evening only.

spots.name: teamLab: Field of Wind, Rain and Sun
spots.blurb: The outdoor teamLab installation near Osaka's eastern edge. Weather itself becomes the medium.
spots.matched: teamLab: Field of Wind, Rain and Sun

spots.name: Osaka Expo 2025 site
spots.blurb: The Yumeshima site. The Expo ended in October 2025; the pin marks the scale of the bet Osaka made on the bay.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市此花区夢洲中一丁目

spots.name: Universal Studios Japan
spots.blurb: The park. Super Nintendo World alone justifies the day: the Mario Kart ride, Power-Up Band blocks, Kinopio's Cafe. Harry Potter, and rotating anime collabs (One Piece, Monster Hunter, Spy x Family). Buy Express Pass early or learn the single-rider lines.

spots.name: Hakutsuru Sake Brewery Museum
spots.blurb: The sake museum in Nada's brewery district. Old wooden tools, free tasting, the smell of fermentation doing half the teaching.

spots.name: Kobe Shushinkan
spots.blurb: The Fukuju brewery in Nada. The shop pours tastings under a cedar ball, the restaurant serves sake lees dishes.
spots.matched: 兵庫県神戸市東灘区住吉南町一丁目８番

spots.name: Nijigen no Mori
spots.blurb: The anime park inside Awaji's prefectural forest. Free entry to the grounds; each attraction zone tickets separately. This is the reason the island is on the route.
spots.matched: Naruto x Boruto park Nijigen no mori

spots.name: Naruto x Boruto park
spots.blurb: Shinobi zone in Nijigen no Mori. A real Hidden Leaf with the Hokage faces on the cliff, maze missions, and Ichiraku ramen at the exit.
spots.matched: Naruto x Boruto park Nijigen no mori

spots.name: Dragon Quest Island
spots.blurb: The outdoor Dragon Quest RPG zone. Walk a real map, fight slimes, level a party. Your name on a party roster.

spots.name: Godzilla Interception Operation
spots.blurb: Zip line into the mouth of a life-size Godzilla bust erupting from the ground. Absurd, magnificent, the island's best headline.

spots.name: Godzilla Museum
spots.blurb: The museum beside the zipline. Suits, props, storyboards, seventy years of the King in one hall.

spots.name: Hello Kitty Smile
spots.blurb: The Kitty palace on the west coast. Gallery rooms, projection mapping, a restaurant facing the strait.

spots.name: Hello Kitty Show Box
spots.blurb: The Kitty show restaurant up the road. Lunch service with a stage show. The roof is a giant Kitty face visible from the air.
spots.matched: 兵庫県淡路市野島平林

spots.name: Awajishima Onion Kitchen
spots.blurb: The burger stand at Uzunooka by the Naruto bridge. Awaji onions on everything, including the onion rings the size of bracelets.
spots.matched: 兵庫県南あわじ市福良乙

spots.name: Greenarium Awajishima
spots.blurb: The garden-center lunch spot with Awaji produce. Local vegetables, olive beef, a greenhouse you eat inside.
spots.matched: 兵庫県淡路市野島常盤

spots.name: miele the DINER
spots.blurb: The seaside diner by Hello Kitty Smile. Awaji burgers and shakes on the terrace over the water.

spots.name: 168 Gelato Caffe
spots.blurb: Gelato in the Nijigen no Mori corner of the island. Cold sugar after the zipline.

spots.name: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
spots.blurb: Off the island over the longest suspension span on earth. Maiko station sits under the bridge deck; the glass-floor promenade is worth twenty minutes.

spots.name: Kobe Airport
spots.blurb: The island airport on its own island. Twenty minutes from Sannomiya on the Port Liner, then barely an hour in the air. This is the hop home.

spots.name: Haneda Airport
spots.blurb: Land at Haneda, not Narita: thirty minutes from the city. The bags are already at the hotel because you couriered them from Awaji.

spots.name: Akihabara, again
spots.blurb: The buy list gets executed. The kit you passed on at Tamashii, the retro cart at Super Potato, the figure at Radio Kaikan. Second pass through the district with a list and a budget.

spots.name: Nakano Broadway, one more pass
spots.blurb: The grail check. Broadway is where the thing you could not find in Akihabara has been sitting in a glass case since 1997.

spots.name: Tokyo Character Street, the omiyage run
spots.blurb: Last stop before the airport. Twenty character shops in one underground strip, so the gift pile takes forty minutes instead of a day.

spots.name: Phone Booth (Kanda Catholic Church)
spots.blurb: A storm. A phone booth. Denji meets a girl named Reze. She's soaked, she's smiling, and she's the most normal person he's ever talked to. She's also a Soviet-trained assassin with a bomb in her neck.

spots.name: Aoi Building
spots.blurb: The street Reze walks to work. Quiet, residential Jinbocho. Fans have matched the exact building from the manga panels — down to the facade details.

spots.name: Onnazaka (Women's Slope)
spots.blurb: Stone stairs from the 1924 earthquake reconstruction. Reze walks these every day to the café. Fans leave gerbera flowers on the landing — Reze's flower, the symbol of what she and Denji almost had.

spots.name: Trois Bagues Vertes (Café Futamichi)
spots.blurb: The real café that inspired Reze's workplace. Also where Denji waits with flowers on the last day. She never shows. Power does. He eats the flowers.

spots.name: Kanda Catholic Church
spots.blurb: The church near the phone booth. Its quiet European architecture anchors the Jinbocho pilgrimage cluster — five Reze Arc locations within a two-minute walk of each other.

spots.name: Suidobashi / Jinbocho Streets
spots.blurb: Fireworks. A kiss. Then Reze bites out Denji's tongue and transforms. The Bomb Devil. The battle starts in the same streets where they fell for each other.

spots.name: Central Chiyoda (Car Chase)
spots.blurb: Division 4 flees by car. Reze pursues on foot — faster than the vehicle. Aki engages her; Future Devil gives him just enough foresight to survive. Violence Fiend pulls him out at the last second.

spots.name: Nihonbashi / Chūō District
spots.blurb: Typhoon Devil arrives — a grotesque infant brain surrounded by a cyclone. The storm swallows central Tokyo. Angel Devil is nearly torn away by the wind. Aki grabs his bare hand. Two months of lifespan gone. 'Die when I'm not around to stop it.'

spots.name: Tokyo Bay Waterfront
spots.blurb: Reze blows off Denji's arm. He shoots chains from the stumps, wraps them both together, and falls into Tokyo Bay. Reze can't detonate underwater. They sink to the bottom, tangled in each other.

spots.name: Coastline (Morning After)
spots.blurb: Dawn. All three wash ashore. Denji could kill her. He doesn't. 'I would've regretted it.' Reze insists she faked everything. Denji asks: then why didn't you kill me at the school? 'Meet me at the café.'

spots.name: Alley near Café Futamichi
spots.blurb: Reze changes her mind. She turns back toward the café. Rats follow her into the alley and form into Makima. Angel throws spears from the rooftop. The country mouse never made it home.

spots.name: Nerima Station South Exit
spots.blurb: Sea cucumber devil. Denji's first real Tokyo assignment. Power gets scolded by Makima for property damage. The mundane beginning of the worst job in the world.

spots.name: Koun Building (Nerima)
spots.blurb: Power leaps off the building to stomp the sea cucumber devil. Excessive force, zero subtlety. Peak Blood Fiend behavior. The building matches the real Koun Building near Nerima Station.

spots.name: Shibuya Station — Hachiko Exit
spots.blurb: The curtain falls. Civilians are sealed inside the station. Geto's screen sets the trap — Gojo walks in knowing it's a trap, believing he can break it. He's wrong.

spots.name: Shibuya Station — Underground B5F
spots.blurb: Prison Realm activates. Gojo freezes — six minutes of memory flashing through his mind. Geto says 'You're my best friend. The only one.' Gojo Satoru is sealed.

spots.name: Shibuya Hikarie
spots.blurb: Nanami's last stand. Burned beyond recognition, he walks toward Mahito knowing he's dead. 'You've got it from here.' Mahito touches him. Itadori watches.

spots.name: Shibuya Mark City
spots.blurb: Choso corners Itadori here. A fight Yuji should not survive — until Choso sees a false memory of Yuji as his brother and hesitates. Blood Manipulation vs Divergent Fist.

spots.name: Harajuku Station
spots.blurb: Before any of it. Yuji and Megumi sit on the bench waiting for their new teacher. Gojo arrives late, grinning. 'Let's go pick up the third one.' The team that will break the world starts here.

spots.name: Roppongi Hills
spots.blurb: First mission. Nobara proves she belongs — hammer and nails against a cursed womb. Tokyo Tower looms behind her in the OP. This is where she decides she's not going home.

spots.name: Sendagaya Tunnel
spots.blurb: Megumi kneels at the tunnel mouth in the OP, shikigami dissolving around him. In-story: a routine investigation that introduces how Grade 2+ curses operate in Tokyo's infrastructure.

spots.name: Otaguro Park (Suginami)
spots.blurb: Maki puts on the cursed spirit glasses for the first time. The pond is full of low-grade spirits — invisible to anyone without cursed energy. A quiet, creepy scene that establishes the show's rules.

spots.name: Kichijoji Kinema Cinema
spots.blurb: Junpei arc. The rooftop batting cages match the real building. Mahito befriends Junpei here — the cruelest manipulation in the series. Junpei thinks he's found someone who understands him.

spots.name: TMG Building (Shinjuku)
spots.blurb: Tokyo Colony No.1. The twin towers of the Metropolitan Government Building become the landmark inside the barrier. Megumi and Reggie Star fight here — Megumi's domain expansion debut.

spots.name: Shinjuku Café (Geto meeting)
spots.blurb: Geto, Jogo, Hanami, and Mahito sit in a Shinjuku café planning the Shibuya Incident. The scene mirrors a business meeting — four cursed spirits ordering coffee, discussing genocide.

spots.name: Nanami's Former Office (Shinjuku)
spots.blurb: Before Jujutsu High, Nanami was a salaryman. His old office building in Shinjuku. He quit because he realized the mundane world was just as cursed — it just didn't have a name for it.

spots.name: Ramla Hall (Iidabashi)
spots.blurb: After Shibuya collapses everything. Yuki Tsukumo, Yuji, and Choso regroup here. Yuki explains the theory of cursed energy optimization. The adults are gone — these three are what's left of the resistance.

spots.name: Don Quijote Ginza Bridge
spots.blurb: Naoya Zenin hunts Yuji through the Ginza district. Choso intervenes. The Zenin clan's ugliest son vs two brothers who shouldn't exist. Blood techniques paint the bridge red.

spots.name: Kabuki-za Theatre
spots.blurb: Yuta Okkotsu appears — sent to execute Yuji Itadori on Jujutsu High orders. The strongest second-year vs the boy who ate Sukuna's finger. Yuta's been ordered to kill, but he's got a different plan.

spots.name: Celes Wedding Chapel (Shibuya)
spots.blurb: The Gourmet Arc. Tsukiyama lures Kaneki to a 'dinner party' inside a church — where ghouls bid on the right to eat him. The stained glass. The balcony seats. Kaneki's kagune erupts for the first time in public. The Gourmet gets a taste and becomes obsessed.

spots.name: CCG Main HQ (Chiyoda)
spots.blurb: The Commission of Counter Ghoul. Every investigator reports here. Washū family runs it from the top floor — and the Washū are ghouls themselves. The building that symbolizes the lie at the center of the entire series.

spots.name: Ueno Station
spots.blurb: Shirazu and Urie — the Quinx Squad's dysfunctional heart. They meet contacts here in :re. Shirazu is broke, sending every paycheck to his sister's medical bills. Urie is calculating his next promotion. Neither knows how little time Shirazu has left.

spots.name: Museum Café (Model for :re)
spots.blurb: The real café that inspired ':re' — Touka's coffee shop after the timeskip. She builds it as a successor to Anteiku. A place where ghouls and humans can sit together. Haise walks in not knowing why it feels like home.

spots.name: JR Shinjuku East Exit
spots.blurb: Touka and Kaneki. The East Exit crowd. She finds him here in Season 1 — or he finds her. Shinjuku at night, neon and noise, two people who shouldn't exist trying to have a normal conversation about nothing.

spots.name: Yoyogi Park
spots.blurb: Tsukiyama finds Haise here in :re. The Gourmet, emaciated and broken after losing Kaneki, encounters Sasaki in the park. He can smell him — it's Kaneki's body, but the mind is someone else. Tsukiyama weeps. 'It's you. It's really you.' Haise has no idea who this man is.

spots.name: Shinagawa Grand Commons
spots.blurb: The Tsukiyama Family Extermination Operation launches from Shinagawa. CCG musters its forces to wipe out the Tsukiyama estate. Haise leads the operation — ordered to kill the family of a man who loved Kaneki more than anyone.

spots.name: Milky Way Café (Ikebukuro)
spots.blurb: An Ikebukuro café in Noro's territory. Every café in Tokyo Ghoul is a front, a meeting place, or a memorial. In the 16th Ward, you drink your coffee fast and you don't stay after dark.

spots.name: Wako Namiki-Dori Building (Godzilla Minus One)
spots.blurb: The Ginza clock tower that Godzilla takes down in Minus One. Still standing. The intersection below is the film's ground zero.

spots.name: Nakagin Capsule Tower site
spots.blurb: Kurokawa's capsule tower was demolished in 2022. The pin stays as a marker of what the city lost. Some capsules survive in museums.

spots.name: Godzilla Square
spots.blurb: The Godzilla statue in Hibiya Chanter Square, successor to the old one from 1995. He guards the cinema district that made him.

spots.name: National Diet Building (Shin Godzilla)
spots.blurb: Where the cabinet meets as Godzilla approaches in Shin Godzilla. Imposing in person, free tours most days.

spots.name: DevilCraft Kanda
spots.blurb: Chicago deep dish and craft beer in Kanda, saved under the Godzilla flag on the map. Good recovery spot after an Akihabara day.

spots.name: Godzilla Head
spots.blurb: The full-size Godzilla head looming over the Toho Building in Kabukicho. It roars on the hour with light and smoke.

spots.name: Godzilla Store Tokyo
spots.blurb: The official kaiju merch store in Shinjuku Marui. Sixty-five years of monsters on shelves.

spots.name: Square Enix Co., Ltd.
spots.blurb: The headquarters in Shinjuku Eastside Square. The cafe in the same block rotates Square Enix game collaborations.

spots.name: Tokyo Tower
spots.blurb: The 1958 orange tower that Godzilla, Mothra and half of anime have destroyed on film. The view is still the romantic one.
